newsitem.title: USA: US mortgage-backeds mostly flat after inventories.
newsitem.headline: US mortgage-backeds mostly flat after inventories.

text.p: U.S. mortgaged-backed securities tracked Treasuries during tranquil trading on Monday, traders said.
"I think there will be a little action later in the week, but the golf outing really kept things quiet today," one trader said. He was referring to a golf event for dealers.
Pass-throughs opened slightly negative but rose slowly throughout the day, nearly catching up with Treasuries by late Monday afternoon.
A Commerce Department report on July business inventories had little influence, fixed-income analysts said.
Commerce said business inventories rose 0.4 percent in July, compared to no change in June. Economists had forecast a 0.2 percent rise in a Reuters survey on Friday.
By late Monday, pass-throughs were off 1/32 to up 1/32 overall and had come off their earlier lows. The 10-year Treasury note was up 2/32, and the five-year note rested unchanged.
Ginnie Mae and Fannie Mae certificates outperformed Freddie Macs minutely. Traders said selling of FHLMC current coupons may have carried through from Friday.
